original_question: Let S(H) be the manifold of strictly positive density operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, equipped with a monotone Riemannian metric g, the flat m-connection from the natural affine embedding, and its dual e-connection. Which e-autoparallel submanifolds does S(H) admit, or equivalently, for which pairs (rho, V) does there exist an e-autoparallel submanifold through rho with tangent space V?
target_in_paper: Section 6 (Hiroshi Nagaoka), item 2: the open problem of determining the e-autoparallel submanifolds of the manifold of strictly positive density operators, together with its equivalent reformulation in terms of pairs (rho, V). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it has the correct quantum state space, the correct geometric data (a monotone Riemannian metric, the flat m-connection from the natural affine embedding, and the dual e-connection), and it already includes the paper's own equivalent reformulation via a point rho and a linear subspace V of the tangent space. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
missing_details: The paper specifies the ambient affine space for the natural embedding: S is embedded into A, where A denotes the totality of Hermitian operators on H. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The metric g is not a special fixed example such as the SLD metric; the problem is stated for a chosen monotone Riemannian metric g on S, and then e is defined as the connection dual to m with respect to that g. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
In the equivalent formulation, V must be stated explicitly as a linear subspace of the tangent space T_rho S at the chosen point rho. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The existential condition should be stated explicitly: one asks whether there exists an e-autoparallel submanifold M containing rho with tangent space T_rho M = V. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The paper frames the problem as seeking quantum analogues, at least formally, of classical exponential families; that motivation is part of the intended scope. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))

The nearby context also records the main obstruction: the e-connection has nonvanishing torsion, which is why the classification problem is highly nontrivial. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
refined_question: Fix a finite-dimensional Hilbert space H, let S be the totality of strictly positive density operators on H, let g be a monotone Riemannian metric on S, let ∇^(m) be the flat connection on S induced by the natural affine embedding S → A into the real vector space A of Hermitian operators on H, and let ∇^(e) be the connection dual to ∇^(m) with respect to g. Determine the ∇^(e)-autoparallel submanifolds of S; equivalently, characterize all pairs (rho, V) with rho ∈ S and V a linear subspace of T_rho S for which there exists an ∇^(e)-autoparallel submanifold M ⊂ S such that rho ∈ M and T_rho M = V.
equivalent_formulation: Characterize the pairs (rho, V), where rho is a strictly positive density operator and V is a linear subspace of T_rho S, for which there exists an e-autoparallel submanifold of S passing through rho with tangent space V at rho.
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly the quantum density-operator problem in Section 6, item 2. I kept your draft narrow and paper-faithful, and only restored the setup that the paper states explicitly: the embedding S → A into Hermitian operators, the fact that m is the flat connection induced by that embedding, the dependence of e on the chosen monotone metric g, and the precise existential quantifiers in the pair-(rho, V) reformulation. I did not broaden the question to the final sentence's more general Riemannian-manifold variant, because the density-operator version is the paper's primary formulation here. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2509.06989))
